title: Hard: polite and friendly, but not renewing
transcript:
Priya (Acme): Hi Ellen, good to hear from you. How's the team?
Ellen (Harbor): Oh, everyone's great, thank you for asking. And honestly, thank you for the last two years. Your leads have been solid and you've always picked up the phone.
Priya (Acme): That's lovely to hear. What can I do for you today?
Ellen (Harbor): So this is a bit awkward. We've decided not to renew when the contract ends in March. Our new partner owns a call center and wants us to use their in-house leads. It's nothing you did.
Priya (Acme): I appreciate you telling me early. Is there anything that would change the decision?
Ellen (Harbor): I don't think so, it's a partnership thing more than a price thing. But I'd love to stay in touch, and we'll finish the contract properly.
Priya (Acme): Of course. I'll send you the wind-down schedule for the last three months by Friday so nothing gets dropped.
Ellen (Harbor): Perfect. You've been a pleasure to work with, really.

title: Hard: furious about a billing error, but loyal
transcript:
Greg (Summit): Marcus, I am really annoyed. We got charged twice again. That's the second time this year and my bookkeeper is losing her mind.
Marcus (Acme): Greg, I'm sorry. I see the duplicate charge here, eighteen hundred dollars.
Greg (Summit): It's ridiculous. I shouldn't have to check your invoices line by line.
Marcus (Acme): You're right. I'll have the refund issued today and I'll get billing to put a manual check on your account.
Greg (Summit): Look, to be clear, I'm not going anywhere. Your leads are the best we've ever had and my agents love them. I just need billing to stop doing this.
Marcus (Acme): Understood. I'll email you the refund confirmation by end of day.
Greg (Summit): Fine. Thank you. Sorry for yelling, it's been a week.

title: Hard: sarcasm and a deadline
transcript:
Priya (Acme): Hi Tom, how are this week's leads looking?
Tom (BlueOak): Oh, fantastic. Really loving it. Another week where a third of the numbers are disconnected. My agents are thrilled.
Priya (Acme): That's not good. Which days were the worst?
Tom (BlueOak): Monday and Tuesday. Great start to the week, as always.
Priya (Acme): I'll pull those batches and have the data team check the phone validation today.
Tom (BlueOak): Sure, that'll fix everything. Look, I'll give it to the end of the month. If the numbers are still this bad, we'll have a different conversation.
Priya (Acme): That's fair. I'll send you a report on what we found by Thursday.

title: Hard: a competitor called, and the client said no
transcript:
Dana (Acme): Hi Rosa, just checking in on November.
Rosa (Liberty): November's been good. Oh, funny thing, a competitor of yours called me last week offering leads for twenty dollars cheaper.
Dana (Acme): Ah. What did you tell them?
Rosa (Liberty): I told them no thanks. We tried a cheap vendor two years ago and it was a disaster. We're happy where we are.
Dana (Acme): That's good to hear. Anything we should change for December?
Rosa (Liberty): Just send me the holiday delivery schedule so my agents can plan around it.
Dana (Acme): I'll send it over tomorrow.

title: Hard: happy client, but the agency is being sold
transcript:
Marcus (Acme): Hi Ruth, how did October go?
Ruth (Golden Years): Really well, our best month. The leads have been great.
Marcus (Acme): Glad to hear it. Anything coming up we should plan for?
Ruth (Golden Years): Actually yes. I'm retiring in the spring and we're selling the agency. The buyer is a bigger group and they have their own vendors.
Marcus (Acme): Congratulations on retiring. Do you know if they'll keep us on?
Ruth (Golden Years): I honestly don't know. I'll recommend you, but it'll be their decision after the sale closes in April.
Marcus (Acme): Would it help if I put together a one-page summary of your results with us that you can share with them?
Ruth (Golden Years): That would be great. Send it whenever it's ready.

title: Hard: short answers, pulling back
transcript:
Dana (Acme): Hi Sam, thanks for joining. How have the leads been?
Sam (Heritage): Fine.
Dana (Acme): Any problems with contact rates or quality?
Sam (Heritage): Not really.
Dana (Acme): Okay. I noticed you dropped to the minimum volume this month. Anything behind that?
Sam (Heritage): We'll see how things go. I don't really have time for these calls anymore, to be honest.
Dana (Acme): Understood. Would a short email update each month work better than a call?
Sam (Heritage): Sure, do that.
Dana (Acme): I'll switch you to a monthly email starting next week.

title: Hard: frustrated with their own agents, not with us
transcript:
Priya (Acme): Hi Nina, how's everything going?
Nina (Northstar): Honestly, I'm frustrated. Not with you. With my own team. Half my agents aren't calling the leads within the hour, and then they complain the leads are cold.
Priya (Acme): That's a common problem. Speed to lead makes a huge difference.
Nina (Northstar): I know. Your leads are good, the ones who call fast are closing. I just need my people to actually do it.
Priya (Acme): We have a short speed-to-lead training we can run for your agents. I can set it up for next week.
Nina (Northstar): Yes please, that would help a lot.
Priya (Acme): I'll send you some times by tomorrow.

title: Hard: says "cancel", means the opposite
transcript:
Dana (Acme): Hi Leo, I heard you had a question about the contract terms.
Leo (ClearPath): Ha, yes, my new office manager asked how we'd cancel if we ever wanted to. I told her if I were going to cancel, I'd have done it two years ago when everyone else was cheaper.
Dana (Acme): That's kind of you to say.
Leo (ClearPath): It's true. Cancelling isn't on the table. I just want her to have the paperwork for her files.
Dana (Acme): No problem. I'll email her a copy of the contract and the terms today.
Leo (ClearPath): Great, thanks Dana.
